description: Herbal remedies formed an important part of ancient medicine, combining practical experience with religious and traditional beliefs about healing. Physicians, healers, and household practitioners used herbs, resins, oils, wine, honey, vinegar, and other ingredients in poultices, salves, infusions, and washes to treat wounds, reduce pain, ease digestive or respiratory ailments, and combat infection. Greek, Roman, Egyptian, Persian, Indian, Chinese, Celtic, and other medical traditions developed extensive bodies of knowledge about medicinal plants, although their effectiveness varied greatly and treatments were often combined with ritual practices, diet, rest, and surgery.
